reviews.review: it's remarkable how many ideas, and how much of the gameplay of the original release of risk of rain hold up over a decade later. even with the extremely good rerelease / remake, the classic still has a ton of value and is worth your time.
I have too many hours in this game but I just can't stop playing. Highly recommend it.  10 out of 10!

A 2D adventure rougue like, where you're a space delivery dude and your ship wierdly crashed, so now you need to wonder through planets finding teleporters so you can go back to your ship, while using the dropped cargo as you weapons!
The style of the game is amazing, for a 2D game it can really leave u immersed in it, the difference in size of your character and the whole world makes you feel very humbled, challenged and curious!
I love the way the lore is presented through the logs, it's really fascinating and a very nice and subtle way to add story and depth to the game without forcing the player to go through a bunch of cut scenes or view it like a movie, it really puts you more in the shoes of this stranded space dude, trying to figure out the bits and pieces of the world surrounding you through logs and journals

Gameplay wise:
The game feels great to play, it can feel a bit hard to get the hand of kiting, to understand that you need to be patient and not just fight anything u see, to understand that the time really matters and u need to keep moving... But thats the fun of it! getting better and understanding the rules of the world, so you can traverse it. The craziest part of this game, which is what i think sets it apart the most from other rogue-likes, is that you can stack items, which can turn the game upside down in terms of challenge! which feels pretty funny and rewarding, one run you're demolished, another you got a crazy build (like crazy attack speed, or even crazy move speed that makes you traverse the maps in seconds AND I MEAN CRAZY, there is pretty much no cap for your stats), there are also lil bugs in the game which don't really break it as much as make the game more funny (like broken frozen walls), and also hidden maps that let you farm for items, hidden entries that unlock you new items, or characters or game-changing mods (like glass or command)
The different characters you can play with, also make the gameplay feel fresh and different everytime, some items work better in some characters than in others which add another layer of knowledge that you can develop!

Theres love and care in this!
And don't even get me started on the music, DAMN!! Those guitar solos while you're traversing the map? And the hard metal when you're at a boss fight? All while also always giving this spacy sparkly vibe on top of the rock/metal mood, top notch man damn, i'm not even a hard rock dude as much as a soft jazz one, but i LOVE the vibe!
Huge props and respect to Hopoo Games for developing this GEM of a game!
Watching the thumbnails and the trailer and all that really doesn't compare to sitting through and putting just a bit of time to try out this game: the early, figuring out and discovering how the game works and feels part is fun; the mid, gathering the characters, mods and new items is fun; and the late, knowing the gimmcks and pretty much breaking the game with and making crazy builds is fun!!!! And doesn't matter what step you're in, there's always that challenge, there's always that chance of dying for a one shot (cuz u got too confident), a chance of getting lost and losing time, there is always a Risk of Rain. This game really makes you think of how you can tweak the break the world in some ways when you figure it out, but at the end of the day, you will always just be a small part of it, this little dot on a huge cosmic space, winning and losing, rising and falling.
Every step of the way you will have fun, every step of the way you'll feel challenged, and that's how games should feel man.

I love Risk of Rain, thank you for making this game, thank you for the fun times, thank you for the wonder!

Great roguelike with simple mechanics that you can figure out without needing a tutorial. I recommend that you check out the wiki for the items because it's easier to navigate but the details behind each item are in the screen after unlocked

Risk of rain is a great roguelite, it puts you into a new world and you move through different locations in this world, mean while a timer rests above your head indicating that the difficulty is increasing, the goal is to activate a teleporter and fight a boss to get to the next area. 

You have a huge roster of characters to unlock and play  as, each of which introduces lore and new hablities, habilities which fit each character perfectly and these are so different from one another that they keep the game new and fresh even after a long time. 

The co-op aspect of the game also caught my eye and it works perfectly, I think half of my time on this game was spent playing co-op, it is a good time.

The world building in this game is also really good, with each item you unlock you get a description from the POV of the person finding it and the story it tells you about the planet you are in, it really pulls you into trying and collect everything, some of these collecting is done in the form of challenges which also add extra playing hours to the game.

I do have one complaint in the aspect of collecting things, which are the monster logs, they have a very low drop chance and although I really wanted to collect the last two boss monster logs, the farming was getting tedious and I just read them online. I don't see why the monster logs couldn't drop on first kill, as that is when you sight them. But this is a small complaint and overall the game is great.

Honestly, I love this game to bits. It's quite rough around the edges, and (obviously) lacks a lot of the polish and design philosophy of the second, but it's fun. Really fun. It absolutely has flaws, like some mediocre level design, or how tanky most enemies are, their lack of mobility, and how arduous it can be to get rid of them all after a teleporter attack, but at its core, the gameplay is so much fun, and it's a sensory delight to see a thousand different missiles and other items fly off at once and rain down on a bunch of mushrooms and giant jellyfish. The characters are quite varied and unique, and the process of getting enough items at a quick enough pace to get ahead of the curve of the difficulty that ramps up over time is genuinely really exciting, partially due to how much more impactful the elements of time are in this game compared to the sequel. Getting ahead of the enemies and going from just barely making it by the skin of your teeth to becoming an unstoppable force of nature is inherently incredibly satisfying - and even if it weren't - I'd still probably boot this game up once every few months just to hear Moisture Deficit, Surface Tension, or Double ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Rainbow again.

Despite being rough, if you stick with it, it's a highly rewarding game to learn and it holds up in terms of gameplay and how much fun it is, to the point of being absolutely worth checking out on its own merits, beyond potentially wanting to see the origins of its even more beloved sequel.

Still worth an exploration for those who wanna know where it all started. You feel the age, the jank, but it's still a beloved game for me. So much so that I've unlocked everything in it, save for one damn monster logbook: the final boss. Jackass never dropped it, after several victories against them.

But whatever, I won't hold random chance against my sense of completion. Would've been nice if the multiplayer had been updated to modern standards, but otherwise, still a great time.

I'd tell you to buy it on sale, but I say that about every game. No game is worth full price these days, money means less every day. So yeah, buy on sale and have a good 2013 time.
